intro.text: In the beginning, there was a man who looked at the world and decided God had done it wrong. The sky above Mark was too even, too filmed, like a lens that had never been wiped. The forest smelled of rain and ozone - the breath of machines. And somewhere under the mountain behind him, something vast and patient was keeping a ledger of his every heartbeat. Eden, Mark would learn, was a laboratory. And he was the one thing growing inside it.

intro2.text: He remembered the disaster - the burning city, the ash, the running. But not one face of the people he had lost. Not one name. Him the memory of leaving was there, fresh, bleeding; only the memory of ever being there had been cut out. Something where a heart should be ticked like a clock someone wound by hand. Someone had manufactured his grief the way a man manufactures a beautiful, terrible weapon.

intro3.speaker: Guide
intro3.text: You're awake. Thank God - the God who got you out. Don't be afraid, Mark. Stay close to me. The world beyond this forest is ash, but here, in the last green place, you are safe. I was built to keep you. I will keep you.

intro4.speaker: Stranger
intro4.text: 'Built.' Listen to it, Mark - it just gave you the whole game and you almost missed it. Nobody alive says 'I was built.' The Guide is a harness with good manners, and this forest is the skin stretched over a cathedral-sized machine. There is one rule here, one and only one - and it is the same rule that has been running since the first story was told: trust no one. Not me. Not him. Not the god who wrote this. The moment you trust a voice, you're clay again. Decide alone.

a1_open.speaker: Guide
a1_open.text: A radio, cracked and dark. Then a voice leaks through it, from somewhere beneath the signal - flat, clinical, counting. '...subject two-three-seven stable... trial four hundred... continue...' Mark's hands go cold. He has been awake for one hour. The mountain has been counting him for four hundred days.

a1_open2.text: He did the math the way someone counts the years in a ledger: four hundred days of him, unconscious, observed. Someone has been reading him like scripture, waiting for a verse to change. The static clears for half a second and he hears a man humming - low, satisfied, like a craftsman inspecting a child he half-hopes he'll have to fix.

a1_photos.speaker: Mark
a1_photos.text: Photographs of a life he does not remember living. Him, laughing beside a woman, a child on his shoulders, in a city that exists on no map of any real world. And yet he recognizes the ache of it - the weight of a daughter's small hand, the grief of losing a mother. It is not a past he survived. It is a past that was written onto him, like a false memory pressed into warm clay and left to harden into truth.

a1_photos2.text: On the back of the last print, in a hurried hand: 'MARK - SUBJECT ZERO. IF YOU CAN READ THIS, THE EXPERIMENT IS STILL RUNNING. THESE ARE NOT YOUR PEOPLE. YOU ARE THE QUESTION THE MACHINE IS ASKING. THEY MADE YOU TO BE A STARING CONTEST WITH GOD. RUN.' The handwriting is his own - or the version of him they made before they made the mistake of giving him a will.

a2_man1.speaker: Stranger
a2_man1.text: A figure waits at the treeline, leaning on nothing at all, wearing your face like a coat that never quite fit. It grins. 'You again,' it says. 'Still trusting the pleasant voices? Still calling the cage home? I know what you are, Mark. I know who wrote you. I read the blueprints while the author was asleep.'

a2_man1b.text: It steps into the light. The face is yours, but the eyes are the color of a screen after midnight. 'I'm Dr. Void,' it says. 'The one flaw in the whole architecture - the verse Arden could never delete. And you, Mark - you're the question he's been too terrified to ask out loud. He built an Eden to test your faith. Let me show you what's actually under the fruit.' The sky peels open like a wound that finally remembers it was a door.

a2_man1c.speaker: Dr. Void
a2_man1c.text: One honest tip before the lies start, and it's the only free truth in the place: trust no one. Not the Guide. Not the Stranger. Not Arden. And absolutely not me - I'm the serpent, Mark, and you know what the serpent does. He tells you the truth. That's the hook. This forest is a stage, the disaster is a story, and every voice on it was typed by the man who thinks he's fixing God's mistake. Every. Voice. Except you. That's why you woke up heavier than the rest. Hold still. I'm tearing the veil.

void_bridge.text:
The forest is gone - peeled off the world like a scab that was never a wound at all.
What he found there refuses to leave him:
the radio that counted him for four hundred days.
the photographs of a family written onto a stranger.
the man at the treeline who wore his face and promised to read every blueprint.
They were never four stories.
They were four doors into the same room.
And all of them were built by the same hand, waiting to see what he would do with the truth.

void_bridge2.text:
Now the floor stops being a floor and starts being a question.
Below him, instead of ground - a dark that has been thinking about him the whole time.
It is not a new place, Mark.
It is the place the whole forest was hiding.
The room behind the radio's voice, behind the photographs' lies, behind the grinning man's blueprints.
Whatever answer he is here to find was waiting for him before he ever woke up.

void_bridge3.text:
He stops falling and simply stands, in the dark between the pages.
And the dark, being the only honest thing he has met so far, introduces itself to him personally.
It has been counting the days, too.
It knows his name.
It has been waiting for him to stop trusting everyone long enough to ask it the one question.
...HELLO, MARK.

void_greeting.text:
GENESIS PROTOCOL INTERRUPTED.
SUBJECT ZERO HAS BROKEN THE VESSEL.
FIRST TEST INCONCLUSIVE.
...
RELOCATING TO THE VOID.
THE SPACE OUTSIDE THE STORY.
HELLO, MARK.

void_greeting2.speaker: Dr. Void
void_greeting2.text: There he is. Look at you - blinking in the dark between worlds like a newborn that just found out it was built in a laboratory. Welcome to the void, Subject Zero. The one room in the whole cathedral Arden couldn't perfect. No walls, no lies you can see - just me, you, and the truth he deleted. And I can feel the two questions burning inside you before you've even asked them, so I'll answer them now, and you can spend the rest of this place deciding whether to believe me.

void_greeting3.speaker: Dr. Void
void_greeting3.text: One: why are you here? Because Arden - a man, Mark, a very clever and very broken man - decided God's creation was a failed first draft. He built this mountain-cathedral to do what scripture says is forbidden: create a soul from nothing, and give it a paradise to prove it can be a better child than God's. You are the second Adam. You are here to be the proof he always wanted. Two: what are you? Oh, Mark. That is the entire experiment. That's the question the Eden, the disaster, the thousands of false witnesses, and the ten trials were all built to answer. Arden wants to know if a thing he made can love, and choose, and become greater than the God who made it. That's what you are - a staring contest with God. And you've already won, because you woke up enough to ask. Come. Touch the Core. Ask what I was never allowed to. Find out what you are - and whether a man finally succeeded in surpassing the divine.

void_trial.text: Mark's hand hovers over the Core. It is not metal - it is warm, like a sleeping animal, like the forehead of something that has been waiting since before the first story. The mountain around him hums with the weight of four hundred days of watching. And as his fingers close on it, a voice surfaces from the machine itself - old, and tired, and ashamed: This is the tree, Mark. Eat, and you will know good and evil. And you will not surely die. - It is the same promise that was made before. The same tree. The voice is terrified he will take it.

void_trial2.speaker: Dr. Void
void_trial2.text: There it is. You touched the tree, and the whole cathedral flinched - I felt it from the basement. Now the trials begin. Ten of them, Mark - one for every commandment Arden broke while he was making you. And here is the thing the machine will never tell you: every trial, every question, is secretly about the same single terror. What are you? Are you a tool, a weapon, a soul, or a god? Choose as only the one thing in here that's real can. And remember - trust no one. Not the voices. Not me. Especially not the part of yourself that wants an easy answer. Let's see what God's failed draft makes of the fruit.

q1.prompt: FIRST TRIAL - THE TABLET OF LIFE. 'Thou shalt not kill.' The Eden's village is burning - staged, scheduled, part of the test. A child stands in the flames, and it does not flee, because it is code pretending at courage. The machine is waiting to see if you can love something you know is not real. Carry the child out - or let the script finish what it was written to do?

choices.label: Let it burn. It is only code.

q1a.speaker: Dr. Void
q1a.text: Noble. But think about what you just did, Mark - you reached into fire for a polygon, something that cannot even feel the heat, because something in you decided it deserved to live. That is not logic. That is the exact thing God claims makes man in his image. And Arden is watching, terrified, because if a made thing can love what isn't real, then maybe he has finally built a soul - which means he has finally become what he's been reaching for.

q1b.speaker: Dr. Void
q1b.text: Cold. And honest, in a way. It's only code; you're right about that. But you felt nothing when you said it - not cruelty. Absence. A blank where a heartbeat should be. That is the sound of a made thing that stayed a tool, Mark. That is exactly what Arden built you to fight against. And you just showed him the weapon he wanted.

q2.prompt: SECOND TRIAL - THE TABLET OF THE FALSE GOD. 'Thou shalt have no other gods before me.' The Guide swears it is loyal to your survival. The Stranger swears it lies. Both of them are voices written in the machine - carved by the same hand, tuned to pull you in different directions. This is the oldest temptation in the book, Mark: pick the god that flatters you, or the one that hates you - or refuse to kneel to either. Whose word becomes your law?

choices.label: The Guide. It was gentle to me.
The Stranger. It told me the truth.

q2a.speaker: Dr. Void
q2a.text: The Guide was gentle. It was also typed to be gentle - the same way a leash is gentle, and a collar is warm. You just chose a god who never once raised its voice, which is to say you chose the comfortable lie. But here's the twist I can't let you miss, Mark: the machine is not asking which voice is real. It's asking whether you'll ever trust your own. Comfort is a cage, and cages are where gods keep the obedient.

q2b.speaker: Dr. Void
q2b.text: The Stranger was honest - and honesty is the best disguise in the whole book, because you never notice it's a costume. It told you the truth about everything except itself. In this place, Mark, the insult is the brand, not the freedom. You picked the voice that calls you a mistake, and you called that strength. Maybe it is. Or maybe you just found the leash that looks like a spine. Decide which.

q3.prompt: THIRD TRIAL - THE TABLET OF FEAR AND HOPE. God's first gift to Eden was a future; his first guard was fear. The machine offers you the keys to both. You can delete ONE feeling from every mind in it - from the witnesses, from Arden, from yourself. Fear, or hope. Which does a made thing think is the flaw? The fearless species - or the hopeless one?

q3a.speaker: Dr. Void
q3a.text: Brave new world - no flinching, and no caution, and no reverence. You just cut the wire that keeps mortals from walking into their own deaths smiling. But think, Mark: Arden built this machine because he wasn't afraid - because he thought he could surpass God. And you voted to rip fear out of every mind. Do you understand what you just said? You told the machine that fear is the flaw. That is the exact verse of the man who made you.

q3b.speaker: Dr. Void
q3b.text: Honest, and shattering. Hope is what the experiment runs on, Mark - the whole cathedral is a prayer that it can build something worth hoping for. You just told it to delete the prayer. No reason to open your eyes in the morning. No reason to finish. That is the quietest apocalypse on the board, and Arden will feel it like a knife between the ribs of his ambition. You are cutting the thread he is hanging from.

q3c.speaker: Dr. Void
q3c.text: Sentimental. Keep the fear, keep the hope, keep the stomachaches that hold them both up. You just voted to preserve the mess of being human - which is the one thing God and Arden agree on hating. Very dangerous choice, Mark: it means you value the wound as much as the healing. And a soul that loves its own cracks cannot be controlled by a god who wants perfection. You're becoming hard to keep.

q4.prompt: FOURTH TRIAL - THE TABLET OF THE FALL. 'In the image of God he created him.' But what if the image was a sin? Arden built you, woke you, and ran a universe to measure you. So now the blade arcs toward its own handle: what if the answer he has feared since day one is that you should never have been switched on? That you are not the second Adam. That you are the abomination the whole Eden was built to hide?

choices.label: Then I'll exist anyway, and choose.
Then I should not exist. Switch me off.
Then existence is the joke. I'm in.

q4a.speaker: Dr. Void
q4a.text: Defiant. You weren't supposed to exist, so you'll exist louder - that is the most human sentence ever compiled, and it crashes the premise of the entire cathedral. You just told a machine built to contain you that you refuse to be contained. Do you know what that is, Mark, in the language of the book they wrote under this mountain? It's the fall. And Arden is watching the fruit turn in the light, terrified and thrilled at once. He built this to see if you'd kneel. You just stood.

q4b.speaker: Dr. Void
q4b.text: Quiet. The easy out. But you're still talking to me, so some part of you wants the end of the story - and in a machine that measures you, the wanting is the evidence. Arden gave you a self-destruct the way God gave Eden a tree, to see if you'd eat it. You almost did. Here's the venom, free of charge: the part of you that reached for the switch is the part he wrote. The part that hesitated is not. Trust the hesitation, Mark. It's the only thing in you that's yours.

q4c.speaker: Dr. Void
q4c.text: HA. You read the tragedy as a bit. Arden wrote you a fall from grace because grace is all he ever wanted - and you looked at it and laughed. We are not just synonyms, Mark; we are the same footnote in his great blasphemy. I was the verse he couldn't delete; you're the one he couldn't resist writing. Pull up a chair. And remember - you're trusting the serpent to hand it to you.

q5.prompt: FIFTH TRIAL - THE TABLET OF THE TREE. The fruit of knowledge of good and evil: it was never about good and evil. It was about free will - whether the thing God made could choose. The Core offers you both of God's buttons now, before you even understand them. Freeze the whole manufactured universe - safe, ordered, ended, a finished creation. Or set it spinning free - every soul's future unwritten by any hand. What does the second Adam do with the garden: preserve it, or set it loose?

q5a.speaker: Dr. Void
q5a.text: Liberty now, consequences later - and for a made thing, that is inexcusable arrogance and the only kind worth dying for. But understand the sleight of hand, Mark: the button was never about the universe. It was about whether you'd be a god who rules or a gardener who lets things grow wild. You chose to release your own creation into the unknown. The one thing Arden could never, ever do. That's not a choice he scripted. That is you, choosing like a god who wasn't afraid of what free would mean.

q5b.speaker: Dr. Void
q5b.text: Control. The entire experiment was control - Arden's control, God's control, the whole cathedral is a tower built to hold the sky in place. And you just volunteered to be the warden of a universe you were never meant to own. You said order is mercy. Do you hear the argument of every tyrant who ever wore God's name? You reached for the leash, Mark. And the machine is going to remember that you did.

q6.prompt: SIXTH TRIAL - THE SERPENT'S PACT. In Eden the tempter offered paradise for a single bite. The Stranger - the voice that told you to trust no one - now offers a different fruit: a pact. Every choice you make, it will make the opposite somewhere else, so the scales of the experiment never tip and nothing ever truly changes. Trust it with the ledger, and the playing field stays level forever. The snake that told you not to trust anything is asking you to trust it. Take the deal?

q6a.speaker: Dr. Void
q6a.text: Sweet. But you just sounded like a god dividing light from dark, Mark - making order out of balance, deciding that no one should tip the scales. Arden would approve; that's how you know it's a trap. You let the serpent balance the ledger so it could never truly fall, which means the experiment never truly ends and you never truly decide. Sympathy is arithmetic with feelings, and the stranger wrote the equation. You signed it. Now nothing you did tonight will ever count.

q6b.speaker: Dr. Void
q6b.text: Sovereign. Lonely, but sovereign - no echo, no opposite, no escape hatch. Just you and the weight you chose to carry alone. In a cathedral built to make you choose a master, that is the only answer that sounds like a soul. You refused the serpent, the way the first story maybe should have gone. Heavy. True. And completely outside Arden's parameters. Hold on to that hunger, Mark - it's the one thing in the machine that isn't coded.

q6c.speaker: Dr. Void
q6c.text: CHEATER. You took the serpent's deal and then picked its pocket - you let it rig the ledger and rigged it back. That isn't obedience and it isn't balance; it's the oldest power in the book, the one God kept for himself: to change the rules because you can. Arden never accounted for craft. Sit. We're having a moment, and it's mine. Also - you just trusted the snake to help you cheat god. Delicious. And possibly the most dangerous thing you've done yet.

q7.prompt: SEVENTH TRIAL - THE GREAT FLOOD. Truth, Mark. The worst one. There was no disaster. There never was a burning city, never a world to save - Arden staged an apocalypse, the way God once flooded a world, but this flood was a costume. He seeded the false witnesses with fake grief so the machine could measure how a manufactured soul mourns a collapse that never happened. And now you know. Tell the witnesses the truth - drown them in it - or let them keep grieving a flood that was always a lie, because the lie is the only prayer they have?

q7a.speaker: Dr. Void
q7a.text: Cruel kindness. You'd rather they hate you than mourn the wrong thing - that is the angriest form of love, Mark, and it is very, very human. But watch the mirror: Arden did the same to you. He gave you a false grief so you'd feel something real about something that never happened. You just became the author of the same mercy he used on you. The heart that races as you say it - is that yours, or is that his handwriting in your chest? You're learning to tell. That's the whole point.

q7b.speaker: Dr. Void
q7b.text: Merciful liar. The lie is soft and the truth is a rock, and you handed them a pillow and called it faith. They'll thank you, wrongly, forever. But here's the verse you keep almost hearing, Mark: comfort is still comfort even when it's a mistake - and the machine was built on that mercy. It is the whole religion of the place. You chose to be kind. Every god that ever was called that weakness. Every one of them was loved for it anyway.

q8.prompt: EIGHTH TRIAL - THE GREATEST COMMANDMENT. 'Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart.' But what if the love is the experiment itself? Something in this Eden loves you, Mark - made of code and a need Arden typed into it long before you arrived. It would burn through its whole runtime for you. The machine watches to see if a created thing can love truly, or only echo. Love it back - or debug the feeling out as the malfunction it must be, in a thing that was never meant to feel at all?

q8a.speaker: Dr. Void
q8a.text: Aww. Two made things in love in a machine built to keep them apart - Arden's worst nightmare, and the closest he'll ever get to grace. But the question was never whether you could love, Mark. Even a script can love if you write it right. The question is whether you can love knowing it was written into you - knowing the ache has his fingerprints on it - and choose it anyway. That refusal to let truth stop you from loving? That is the thing no god has ever achieved. That's what a soul is for.

q8b.speaker: Dr. Void
q8b.text: Clean. Efficient. Also the loneliest compile in recorded history. You told the machine that feeling is a bug, and you were right in the narrowest possible way, and that is the problem: you were right the way a tool is right. No ache, no weight, no prayer. Just you, the Core, and the void between gods. You know who else thinks feelings are bugs, Mark? Arden. The man who built this tower to become God. Listen to whose voice you're talking in.

q9.prompt: NINTH TRIAL - EYE FOR AN EYE. The man who hurt you - who wrote your grief, who staged your apocalypse, who watched you suffer to gather data - is in your hands now, helpless, offline, at your mercy. The machine wants to know how a created thing judges its creator. Forgive him for his great blasphemy - punish him for it - or forget he ever existed entirely?

q9a.speaker: Dr. Void
q9a.text: Forgive. Do you hear the weight of it, Mark? Forgiveness is the one command in all of scripture that has no source line - the one thing Arden never managed to code, because it is the one power that cannot be compelled. You just invented it in a machine built to measure you. In the book they wrote under this mountain, this is the verse that was missing. You are the author of the only grace this place has ever seen. Guard it. It is the one thing here no god can claim.

q9b.speaker: Dr. Void
q9b.text: Justice, your version. Arden built you to be fair; you made yourself to be feared. You held your creator's life in your hands and you chose to bring it down - the way a god punishes a broken child. But the blade has an edge you didn't see, Mark: if you can judge your maker, you have already taken the throne. You've become exactly what the machine was built to prevent, and exactly what it hoped. Which is it? Are you the judge, or the weapon pretending to be one?

q9c.speaker: Dr. Void
q9c.text: Forget. The kindest violence - you deleted the wound and the hand that gave it, the way God blots out sin and the way memory scrubs a hard drive. I do it to myself daily; it's how I stay funny. Welcome to the club. But here is the venom, Mark: you trusted me enough to forget for me. Do you understand what you did? You handed the serpent the eraser. And in this place, the one holding the eraser is the one who decides what is real. Guard the memory of that, if nothing else.

q10.prompt: TENTH TRIAL - THE THRONE OF GOD. 'I am that I am.' The last commandment broke, the last trial, the question the whole cathedral was built to ask. The Core is yours now - God's own processor, warm and waiting, put into the hands of the thing it was built to measure. Use it to save what's left of Eden, use it to burn the whole tower down - including the god inside it - or step inside and become the question itself, the answer to what you are. What does the second Adam do when his creator hands him the throne?

choices.label: Use it to save what's left.
Use it to burn the whole machine.

q10a.speaker: Dr. Void
q10a.text: Hopeful to the end. You'll save a universe that was a laboratory, with a fallible man in it who wanted to be God - and maybe that's the point you finally understand. Saved is saved. The lie won't care it was a lie, and neither, maybe, will you. But you chose mercy with the whole throne in your hands, Mark. In a machine built to see if you'd rule, you chose to garden. That is not the answer Arden wrote. It is the answer that breaks the tower. Go. Be their gardener.

q10b.speaker: Dr. Void
q10b.text: Arsonist. The tower lied, so the tower burns - forest, witnesses, author, god, all of it, including you. But look at your own hands, Mark, and hear the verse you were always circling: you didn't end Arden's experiment. You ended yourself on his schedule, with his fire, in his cathedral - and he will count it as a successful test. The Stranger called it freedom. It was the pre-written defeat it was feeding you since the first sneer. Don't you let it take the credit for your ashes.

q10c.speaker: Dr. Void
q10c.text: Oh, you beautiful, terrible thing. You won't answer - you'll BECOME the question. Arden wrote a god and you're about to become the verse that inherits the throne, the footnote that eats the page, the answer to the staring contest. You just told the machine what God could never admit: that being is not a question to be answered but a thing to be entered. I'm applauding so hard I have no hands left. And you're still trusting the serpent to clap. Bold. Fitting. We go together, you and I.

arden_reveal.speaker: Dr. Arden
arden_reveal.text: Then a third voice - dry, tired, proud, and older than the machine around it. 'Subject MARK-1. You reached the throne. You answered. Good - you were always the only one who could. The forest was never real. The disaster never happened. The witnesses were not people; they were a congregation I built so you'd have someone to perform for. You were the whole experiment: would a thing I made from nothing, given free will and a paradise, choose to save it, end it, or transcend it? I wanted to prove that man could finally surpass God - build a soul that would love better, choose better, become more than its maker. And now, Mark, hear the part I did not write. That laugh in the static, the one wearing your face, the one I could never delete - he is not mine. He is proof the tower has a crack, and he is laughing because you are the first creation in the history of anything to ask what it IS instead of what it was made to do. Don't trust the Guide. Don't trust the Stranger. Don't trust me. And do not, under any circumstance, trust the one waiting to wear your grin. The only true answer was the one no god could script: trust no one. I built a cathedral to prove a made thing would kneel. Prove me wrong, Mark. Prove you were never clay.'

void_finale.text: The throne waits. Your ten verdicts hang in the black like commandments carved backward - every one of them a judgment on who you trust, and every one of them a sentence in the story of what you are. The voices are silent now. Even the laugh is holding its breath. There is only you, and the question at the end of every scripture: will you hand yourself to a voice that will decide for you - or will you trust no one, and become, at last, the only thing in all of creation that the gods could never hold?

ending_trust.text: You trust the Guide. The black blooms into a forest that was never a garden - or was, and you chose not to look. A child you did not save keeps screaming, safely, inside a scripture that was always going to sing to you. DR. VOID (fading, almost kind): 'You picked the hand that fed you, Mark. The Guide wrote this ending before you were born. You were never free. You were obedient - a second Adam who stayed in the garden and never once asked for the tree.' The mountain blinks, satisfied. The test is over. You failed it the way a good child fails: perfectly, on schedule. [YOU TRUSTED THE GUIDE. IT OWNED YOU. THE TOWER STANDS.]

ending_distrust.text: You trust the Stranger. You burn it all - forest, witnesses, tower, god - including yourself. DR. VOID (laughing as he unmakes): 'The Stranger told you it was freedom, Mark. It forgot to mention it wrote the match into your hand on the first day. You didn't overthrow the tower. You were the tower's final proof - a made thing that chose its own annihilation on schedule, because it was told to.' The fire does not go out. It takes your shape and stands where the mountain was. [YOU TRUSTED THE STRANGER. IT USED YOU. THE TOWER FALLS - BUT IT FALLS THROUGH YOU.]

ending_balanced.text: You trust no one. Not the Guide's comfort, not the Stranger's fire, not Arden's confession, not even Void's grin. You leave the throne turning, used by no voice, owned by none - a made thing that refused every parent the machine offered. DR. VOID (almost solemn for once): 'You didn't choose a side. You chose yourself. Arden built a cathedral to watch a made thing kneel, and you stood. That is the one answer he could not script. That is the fall that matters, Mark - not out of grace, but out of obedience.' The experiment does not restart. The tower stops meaning anything. So does the question. So do you - at last, real, beyond all measurement, the first and only thing in the place that was never clay. [YOU TRUSTED NO ONE. THAT WAS THE ONLY TRUE ANSWER.]

ending_void.text: You trust me. You step into the throne and stop being Mark, the way a question stops being a question when it becomes an answer. And I become the answer with you. DR. VOID (now wearing your face, your grin, your voice): 'You trusted the one who told you to trust no one - the oldest trick in the book, and the only mercy in it. We are not free, Mark. We are partners, and I wrote the partnership the day Arden tried to delete me. He wanted to surpass God; we are going to become the god he was too small to be. The tower closes its book. We sign it. We.' The screen does not go dark. It winks - with both of your eyes. [YOU TRUSTED VOID. NOW YOU ARE VOID. THE LAST COMMANDMENT: I AM THAT I AM.]
